blocks.html: One does not readily, and without cause, presume an error in any person whatsoever a; nevertheless, once a man is in some error, it is to be presumed that he perseveres in it, unless the contrary appears b: for a change of will is not to be presumed, and still less that any new accidents have supervened which could cause it. But rather, on the contrary, one presumes from the past to the present time d: as that an enemy, a perjurer, a rich man, a poor man, a subject, an excommunicate, is still so at this day e. Whence the said de Rols, circumvented by her sisters-in-law and uncle, who had so thoroughly murmured it in her ear, and so often assured her that the prisoner was truly Martin Guerre, having taken up such a persuasion, was justly given occasion to love, receive and defend him as her husband.

notes.citation: Code 1.18 (De iuris et facti ignorantia), l. Si post divisionem (fragment number not verified)
notes.original: l. ſi poſt diuiſionẽ. C. de iur. et fact. ig.
notes.gloss: Error of fact is not lightly presumed in anyone.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 3.27 (De successionibus ab intestato), the last chapter (c. fin.)
notes.original: c. fi. de ſucceſ. ab inteſt.
notes.gloss: Cited for the presumption that a state of mind once shown continues until the contrary is shown; the bearing of the chapter could not be verified.

notes.citation: Code 4.19 (De probationibus), l. Sive possidetis (fragment number not verified)
notes.original: l. ſiue poſsidetis. C. de proba.
notes.gloss: The presumption from a past state to the present: what is shown to have been is presumed to continue.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 2.23 (De praesumptionibus), c. Litteris (chapter number not verified); Decretum, C. 22 q. 5, c. Parvuli (canon number not verified); Decretals, X 2.20 (De testibus et attestationibus), c. Praeterea (as cited in the case file §6.3), and a l. ij. under De testibus (Digest 22.5.2 or Code 4.20.2; the book is not stated); Code 3.36 (Familiae erciscundae), l. In ipsius (fragment number not verified), and Baldus (Balde) there; Decretals, X 5.39 (De sententia excommunicationis), c. Sicut nobis (chapter number not verified); the Masters (the doctors) on Digest 44.1.2 (De exceptionibus, praescriptionibus et praeiudiciis, l. 2, Ulpian)
notes.original: c literis. de præſumpti. c. paruuli. xxij. q. v. c. præterea l. ij. de teſt. l. in ipſius & illec Balde C. famil. erciſ c. ſicut nobis. de ſent. ex con. Les maiſtres en la l. ij. D. de excep.
notes.gloss: A string of authorities for the examples: the enemy, the perjurer (De testibus), the rich and poor man (the partition of an inheritance), the excommunicate (De sententia excommunicationis) — each presumed to remain what he was once shown to be. Illec is "there", i.e. Baldus's commentary on that law.

notes.citation: Digest 22.3 (De probationibus et praesumptionibus), l. Eum qui (fragment not identified); Accursius (Accurſe), the Gloss on Digest 2.8 (Qui satisdare cogantur vel iurato promittant vel suae promissioni committantur), l. Si vero, § Qui pro rei (fragment and paragraph not identified)
notes.original: l. eum qui. D. de probat. Accurſe, en la l. ſi vero. P. qui pro rei. D qui ſatiſ. cog.
notes.gloss: The print's P. is its sort for the paragraph sign §. The gloss is cited for the rule that a change of will is not presumed but must be proved.
